title: Why the Ocean Looks Blue
post_title: Why the Ocean Looks Blue | QuantaTale
post_description: The ocean isn't simply reflecting the blue sky. Water itself changes the light. Discover the science behind it. Sources: https://oceanservice.noaa.gov/facts/oceanblue.html https://www.usgs.gov/water-science-school/science/water-color #Science #ScienceFacts #Education #QuantaTale
narration: Why does a deep ocean often look blue? Water absorbs the red end of visible light more strongly, while more blue light remains available to reach our eyes. That is different from the process that makes the sky blue. And not every ocean is the same colour: sediments, tiny organisms and dissolved materials can shift the water toward green, brown or other shades. The colour is a clue to how light interacts with water.
